messages:
maya: heads-up — just finished the e2e comparison run: replay harness vs synthetic steady-rate for streaming and non-streaming. results look... interesting.

sam: cool, what's the setup? batch sizes / kernels / kv state?

maya: replay harness (trace from prod load test, 12k reqs over 10m) vs synth (poisson arrivals, mean 20 qps). both: model=redwood-7b-qat, seq=1024, clients=100, warmup=2m, run=8m.

jorge: did you toggle kernel selector? we saw different perf for fwd-kernel-v2 vs compat-path.

maya: yes. toggle matrix: kernel=auto / force-fast-attn / compat. batching heuristic: dynamic (latency SLO 300ms) vs fixed (batch=8 / 16 / 32). KV cache: cold start vs warmed (replay preserves KV across segments).

linus: nice. TL;DR numbers?

maya: summary:
- replay + streaming + kernel=auto + dynamic batching = best p95 latency but higher GPU utilization (70->86%).
- synthetic + non-streaming + fixed batch=32 + compat kernel = best throughput but p95 latency exceeds 300ms on tail spikes.
- forcing fast-attn kernel regresses for streaming for short chunks because of increased host->device memcpy overhead.

sam: can you paste the perf table / key metrics?

maya: pasted below (abridged):
```
scenario, p50(ms), p95(ms), qps, gpu_util
replay/streaming/auto/dyn, 42, 218, 180, 86%
synth/nonstream/compat/b32, 58, 412, 320, 74%
replay/nonstream/fastattn/b8, 50, 290, 210, 79%
```

jorge: interesting that replay qps is lower — probably backpressure from client read loop. any profile traces?

maya: perf-bot attached CPU/GPU timeline and nvprof snippets. main takeaway: streaming path has more frequent small kernel launches; kernel selector often picks fast-attn but per-launch overhead + memcpy kills short-chunk cases. also KV cache lookups are cheap, but cache misses cause unexpected stalls due to synchronous load of chunked KV pages.

perf-bot: @here profiling artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/replays/1766001234/ (cpu.svg, nvtx.json, kernel_choices.csv)

sam: did you try batching heuristic that respects client read-window (so we avoid tiny chunks across network)?

maya: yes — added a min_chunk_window=64 tokens which aggregated streaming chunks into fewer larger kernels; p95 improved ~25% for streaming with fast-attn forced.

linus: any regressions vs last week's baseline (1765500000 run)?

maya: two: 1) compat kernel got a 10% slower l2 read after a driver update -> we saw throughput drop in fixed-batch tests. 2) a subtle regression in the replay harness where kv warmup phase wasn't replaying prefix caching consistently — inflated cold-miss rate. opened issue #ENG-872.

jorge: can you share the exact harness commands so we can reproduce? also want to try a replay that coalesces client reads (simulate smarter client loop).

maya: commands:
```
./harness/run_replay --trace s3://traces/2026-03-01/replay1.json --model redwood-7b-qat --streaming yes --kernel auto --batching dynamic --min_chunk_window 64
./harness/run_synth --qps 20 --clients 100 --model redwood-7b-qat --streaming no --kernel compat --batch_size 32
```

sam: perfect. i'll run with driver pinned to older version to bisect compat l2 change.

replay-bot: replay-bot reports: backpressure events during replay at t=00:03:14 - queue depth spiked to 42, client read-latency 180ms.

maya: note: the best apples-to-apples is to align workload shape — replay trace we used has heavier prefix reuse, synth has none. after modifying synth to mimic prefix reuse (warm-kv segment), synth streaming results moved closer to replay.

linus: action items?

maya: 1) bisect driver regressing compat L2 (sam)
2) fix replay harness kv-warmup so prefix caching is stable (maya)
3) experiment: client read loop coalescing in streaming client (jorge)
4) add min_chunk_window heuristic to runtime and gate by perf flag (eng-runtime release candidate)

jorge: added tasks in eng-runtime board. thanks — can we keep follow-ups in this thread so perf artifacts are linked?

sam: :thumbsup: 

replay-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/feature/min_chunk_window -> canary in 30m

maya: i'll post the final perf tables + flamegraphs here once bisect completes. :eyes:
